newsitem.title: USA: Stocks off slightly, pausing for breather.
newsitem.headline: Stocks off slightly, pausing for breather.

text.p: Wall Street stocks hesitated in their two-week surge Monday, with technology shares succumbing to profit-taking and blue chips posting mild losses at midday.
At 1 p.m. EST the Dow Jones industrial average was off 12.30 points at 6,335.73, pausing after racing on Friday to its eighth consecutive record high close.
Last week, the blue-chip index climbed 128.21 points after jumping 198 point in the earlier week amid low inflation and declining long-term interest rates.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances by a small margin on modest volume of 211 million shares.
The technology-laden Nasdaq Composite Index was off 10.14 points at 1,251.66, and the American Stock Exchange index was off 1.51 points at 583.90.
"Techs are taking a breather and it's a long overdue breather," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.

Analysts said, however, the respite appeared to be a temporary one in an overall uptrend that has seen stocks rally furiously since Election Day, adding some 300 points to the Dow and pushing virtually all major indices to repeated record highs.
"We probably should see some profit-taking at this point," said Peter Canelo, chief investment strategist at Dean Witter. "You don't see too many two-week periods like this."
He added, "If the market consolidates now, it could lose about a third of its gains since Election Day."
Among the technology stocks backtracking were International Business Machines Corp., off 1-3/8 to 143-5/8, Intel Corp., down one to 144-7/8, and Cisco Systems Inc., down 1-9/16 to 63-3/16.
Mergers and other special situations dominated the otherwise quiet session, topped by a 60 percent surge in Tyco Toys Inc., which jumped 4-1/4 to 11-1/4 after agreeing to be acquired by Mattel Inc.
Mattel, which will pay $12.50 in stock for each Tyco share in a deal valued at more than $750 million, was off 7/8 to 29-3/4.

Tosco Corp., which agreed to purchase Unocal Corp.'s 76 Products Co. refining and marketing business, rose 9-7/8 to 70. Tosco said it would pay $1.4 billion for the unit's assets, assume limited environmental liabilities and make additional payments to Unocal based on future profits.
Unocal, which had been seeking a buyer for the 76 Products unit for some time, climbed 1-1/8 to 40-5/8 on news of the deal.
McDonnell Douglas Corp., which fell from contention in a three-way competition to build a next-generation fighter jet, skidded five points to 51-3/4.
The shares of the remaining two competitors posted solid gains, with Boeing Co. rising 2-5/8 to 94-3/8 and Lockheed Martin Corp. up 2-1/8 to 95-7/8.
